title: The best reason to care about Nvidia’s RTX Spark: ‘everything’ will run on Arm
key_facts: Nvidia's first RTX Spark laptops go on sale Friday 16 Oct, running full Windows 11 on an Arm-based chip, using Microsoft's Prism emulator for older apps.
Justin Walker, Nvidia senior director of products, said 'all your apps, all your games, everything's going to run great'.
Nvidia says it supports anti-cheat software for Fortnite, Roblox, Rust and others, with Call of Duty, Valorant and more coming later.
Verge testers found some CPU-bound games stuck at about 30fps; graphics power is akin to a midrange RTX 5060 laptop GPU.
Prices: Surface Laptop Ultra from $2,600 up to $5,900 for 128GB of memory; Verge calls it expensive partly because memory prices have soared.
The RTX Spark chip is the same one Nvidia put in AI developer mini desktops a year ago, which ran Linux.
quote_evidence: "All your apps, all your games, everything's going to run great on Spark," Nvidia senior director of products Justin Walker told journalists last week.
The reality is that some "CPU-limited" games will run slower because Microsoft's Prism has to convert their x86 instructions to Arm instructions in real time
why_it_matters_hint: If Windows apps and games run well on Arm, Nvidia and Qualcomm laptops become more real rivals to Intel, AMD and Apple.
notes: Verge opinion piece with early hands-on testing; Nvidia claims noted as claims.
